1. PRELIMINARY
1.1 Objectives
The primary objective of this framework is to supplement and facilitate the enforcement of Section
3 of the Prudential Regulation 2024, and Sections 234 - 241 of the Financial Services Act 2011.
This framework establishes maximum limits and prudential requirements for the regulatory
oversight of financial institutions' exposures to a single counterparty or a group of connected
counterparties.
1.2 Title, Commencement and Application
This framework shall
(a) be called the Large Exposure Framework, hereafter referred to as LEF 2025.
(b) come into effect from 1st July 2025
(c) apply to all FIs regulated by the Royal Monetary Authority
(d) be reviewed and amended from time to time.
2. LARGE EXPOSURE
2.1 Definition
Large exposures shall mean those exposures of a FIs to an individual borrower or a group of
connected borrowers, which is equal to or more than 10 percent of the Tier I capital based on the
latest audited balance sheet.
2.2 Computation of large exposure
As stated in section 3.2.2 of PR 2024, the FIs shall consider the following to compute large
exposures:
(a) Term loan: outstanding balance
(b) Overdraft facilities: sanction amount or outstanding balance whichever is higher
(c) Off-balance sheet items: off-balance amount less margin money

2.3 Maximum limit on large exposures
(a) Exposures to any single company, public corporation, firm, association of persons, or an
individual shall not exceed 25 percent of the FI’s Tier I capital in line with section 3.4.4(i) of
PR 2024
(b) The following exposure shall be aggregated and shall not exceed 30 percent of the Tier 1
Capital in line with section 3.4.4(ii) of PR 2024.
i. an individual, his close relations or a company or firm in which he or his close relations
have a substantial interest; or,
ii. a group of connected borrowers if at least one of the following criteria is satisfied:
1. Control relationship: in assessing whether there is a control relationship between
counterparties, financial institutions must consider these criteria if one entity owns
more than 10% (significant owner) of the shareholding of the other entity. In addition,
financial institutions must assess connectedness between counterparties based on
control using the following criteria:
(a) is able to appoint or remove the majority of board of directors or management of
the other;
(b) is able to cast the majority of votes at meetings of the board, general meeting or
equivalent governing body of the other;
(c) is able to direct the activities of the other so as to obtain benefits from its activities;
and
(d) commonality of ownership and management
2. Economic interdependence: in establishing connectedness based on economic
interdependence, FIs shall consider, at a minimum, the following criteria:
(a) having the same expected source of repayments

(b) an individual, his/her spouse and economically dependent children;
(c) where one counterparty has fully or partly guaranteed the exposure of the other
counterparty;
(d) where it is likely that the financial problems of one counterparty would cause
difficulties for the other counterparty in terms of full and timely repayment of loan
liabilities
(e) where the insolvency or default of one counterparty is likely to be associated with
the Insolvency or default of the other; and
(f) significant association or relationship exists among counterparties, e.g. sharing of
common marketing and/or branding platform etc.
2.4. Disaggregation of exposures
In line with section 3.3.4 of PR 2024, a FIs may disaggregate its exposures for computation of
the large exposures limit if the following criteria are met:
(a) a single borrower or such connected person has sufficient financial resources of its own to
obtain credit facilities and to fully service its liabilities; and
(b) a single borrower or such connected person is not relied upon to support the liabilities of the
other or other persons connected to the counterparty out of its financial resources.
2.5. Exclusions of exposures
In line with section 3.4.5 of PR 2024, the following exposures shall be excluded from the
computation of large exposures:
(a) inter-bank exposures with a maturity of three months or less;
(b) exposures fully covered by cash collateral;
(c) exposures covered by government guarantees;
(d) exposures to governments and the central banks.

2.6. Maximum limit on total large exposures
In line with section 239 of FSA 2011, the sum of its large exposures shall not exceed 8 times of
Tier 1 capital.
2.7. Prudent requirement
In pursuant to section 3.8 of PR 2024 on the general requirement, the policy on large exposure
shall include the following but not limited to:
(a) Internal Risk Appetite
Defining risk appetite to align their risk exposure with their financial capacity and strategic
objectives, preventing excessive risk-taking.
(b) Internal Risk Tolerance limit
Clear risk tolerance thresholds for not exceeding acceptable risk levels, safeguarding against
potential financial instability from large exposures.
(c) Early Warning System
An early warning system to provide prompt detection of emerging risks, allowing timely
intervention before issues escalate into significant losses.
(d) Escalation Process
A defined escalation process to ensure critical risks are promptly communicated to senior
management and the Board for swift decision-making and action.
(e) Risk Mitigation Plan
i. A risk mitigation plan to outline strategies to reduce potential risks, ensuring the institution
is prepared to manage and minimize adverse impacts from large exposure.
ii. As required by section 114(i) of CGRR 2024, the large exposures must be reviewed by the
Risk Management Function
iii. As required by section 127 of CGRR 2024, the large exposure must be audited by the
internal audit every quarter and submit the report to the Authority also in line with section
3.4 (iv) of PR 2024 to ensure compliance to the prudential limit and standards/internal
policies;
Page 4 of 6

iv. The FIs shall conduct stress tests and scenario analyses to determine how their large
exposures will perform under adverse economic conditions to prepare for unexpected
shocks.
v. As per section 240 of FSA 2011, FIs will report to Authority within 7 days risk after
reaching the risk tolerance limit.
vi. A financial institution that fails to comply with any of these regulations, shall be liable to
the penalties in line with section 241 FSA 2011, Thus, Non-compliance shall be fined as
per the Penalty Rules and Regulations 2022 and amendment thereof
vii. Additionally, FIs shall assign risk weight of l50% for capital adequacy computations in the
event of the exposures exceeding the maximum limits
3. OTHER REQUIREMENTS
3.1. Regulatory reporting and monitoring
(a) FIs shall submit the report to authority on large exposures on a monthly basis as per the Annex
I.
(b) The Authority shall monitor the adherence to the provisions of the framework through its
regular on-site- inspection and off-site surveillance of the regulated entities;
(c) The Authority shall take supervisory actions against the regulated entities' non-compliance
with these Guidelines.
